texts: good. the full-moon state is reified and anchored to the date, with the flat past copular emitted beside it so a plain 'was the moon full?' still answers. One caveat no rewrite can fix: our day term is a day-of-month slot, so a day counted within a year ('day 640') may not order against other dated events - that is a limitation on our side, not a reason to reword.

good. the saying reifies with Old Vesh as its holder and the reported clause is sealed under it, with the Council and the definite 'the village' typed at top level and nothing about the cycle asserted as fact.

mixed: the saying and the lessons-became-policies shape are right, but 'the lessons of Year 1' and 'the policies of Year 2' put a calendar period in a possessor slot, which our notation only licenses as a time filler - so each year is recorded in a place nothing else can match, and neither joins up with the same period used as a date elsewhere in the passage. Rewrite so each year sits on an event as a time adjunct: 'Meren Tallowhand said at the Council that the lessons the village learned in Year 1 had become its policies in Year 2.' (this names the village as the learner, which sentence 2 has already established).
good. the closing reifies with the Council as the doer, the meeting as the thing closed and the phrase as the means, and the phrase witness it mints is exactly the one sentence 6 reuses.

bad: 'for the first time' comes out as a rank atom meaning she was the first person ever to attend the Council - not what you wrote - and there is no licensed way to say 'the Nth time this person did X', so a correct parse would simply drop the phrase and the fact would be lost either way. State the prior non-attendance outright instead: 'Coraline Ash was a Keeper, and she attended the Council; she had never attended the Council before.' ('as a Keeper' itself came through fine, as a typing atom on Coraline.)
good. the repeating reifies with Coraline as the doer and reuses sentence 4's phrase witness, so the two mentions of the phrase are one thing.
